lesson.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specAnchors.text: understand how platelets are involved in blood clotting, which prevents blood loss and the entry of micro-organisms

primer.text: Cut a finger and, within minutes, a soft plug hardens into a scab that keeps blood in and germs out. The workers behind that repair are platelets — cell fragments that trigger a chain reaction in the plasma. This note walks the clotting cascade step by step.

modules.title: Platelets and the Clotting Cascade
modules.opening: Platelets are cell fragments that converge on any wound, where a cascade in the plasma turns soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin, traps red cells into a clot, and dries it into a protective scab.
keyPoints: Platelets are fragments of cells, not whole cells.
They release chemicals that convert fibrinogen into fibrin.
Fibrin forms an insoluble mesh across the wound.
Trapped red blood cells complete the clot.
The dried clot becomes a scab that blocks micro-organisms.

low.restatement: Platelets arrive, fibrin meshes over the gap, red cells get trapped, and a scab dries in place.
low.analogy: Rebar and concrete: fibrin is the mesh, trapped cells are the aggregate, the scab is the set slab.
low.examPointer: Keep the pair straight: fibrinogen soluble first, fibrin insoluble second.

medium.restatement: The two-fold purpose is stopping blood loss and sealing the wound against micro-organisms until new skin grows beneath.
medium.analogy: Sandbagging a leaking riverbank while the repair crew rebuilds behind it.
medium.examPointer: Exams reward the protective pairing: blood loss AND pathogen entry, both stated.

glossary.definition: Cell fragments that trigger the clotting cascade at a wound.
The soluble plasma protein converted into fibrin during clotting.
The insoluble mesh protein that traps cells into a clot.
The dried, hardened clot sealing a healing wound.
